title: Charles III of Lorraine to the comte de Vaudémont, Nancy, 18 June 1592, BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (DECODE R9449)

steps.what: Verify step: looked for the ciphered originals of the January intercepts in fr. 3621; no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment only, no cipher in the volume to pair it with.
Key sought in DECODE (8 records for fr. 3621), Cryptiana, HistoCrypt, BnF notices, Lepage 1864: none published; other Lorraine keys are different systems.
Four 1592 key sheets in fr. 3995 whose DECODE profile matched (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) fetched and eliminated on their own evidence.
Shear-deskew line finder segments 20 lines / 1,114 glyphs; clear text of nos. 22 and 97 transcribed; unsupervised shape clustering of the glyphs.
Homophonic annealer (solve.py) against a Montaigne 4-gram model on the clustered glyphs: -2.78/char against -1.85 for real French.
Glyphs recognised as ordinary cursive letterforms and transcribed by eye from 42 half-line crops: 1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms and 38 figures (ct/no97_eye.txt).
Old annealer on a control with a known key recovers only 37-56% (true key -1.62 vs found -2.64): the search, not the model, had failed.
Steepest-ascent iterated local search (search.py) recovers known keys at 98.7-99.6%; free nulls and degenerate all-e keys identified as traps and blocked.
Search on the manuscript: key stable across seeds and under a locked crib, -2.10/char; words produced unprompted (munitions, prisonniers, secours, quartiers, conserver la plaine).
Eight-symbol group reading 'chasteau' at lines 15 and 19, with Chasteauvillain twice in the clear on the page; one symbol short (chasteauilains), so eight letters secure and six probable.
Null test: same pipeline on five shuffled ciphertexts gives 0-3 distinct French words of 6+ letters (mean 1.2) against 33 for the manuscript.
Noise and systematic-merge controls: the -2.10 score matches 6-12 merged glyph pairs, i.e. about 65-75% of letters correct; the transcription limits the reading.

The 18 Sept key's values pair reciprocally (a/i, o/r, d/q, n/s); tested as an 11-pair reciprocal alphabet a/i b/p c/f d/q e/t g/u l/y m/z n/s o/r h/x with the transcription's c split into e (t) and c (f), B into b (p) and h (x), dots = doubled letter, ae = null: lowercase-only decode turns into French (infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution; conserver la plaine).

Native IIIF image of f227 sheared -0.031, 21 line bands cut into 5 crops each at 2.3x; every cipher line re-read against the pair key, glyph choices (e/c, b/h, dotted forms) decided with the key in hand; word-graded transcription ct/no97_reread.txt (1,105 tokens).
Nomenclator figures from context: 31 = ma (com-31-nder, de-31-nde, 31 resolution), 139 = vous (chemins, 139 tiendres), 145 = me (affin que 141 ne 145 delaissent); the other 11 figures unassigned.
fr. 3621 notice searched for sibling Lorraine/Vaudemont cipher pieces: none (ciphered pieces are Birago 31/36, Potier 79, Dinteville 114/116).

measure_reread.py: 790/1,105 cipher tokens in words graded H/C = 0.715 (letters 0.721, figures 21/38); the 18 Sept key+tokens give the same words for 449/1,105 = 0.406; 4 emendations (two omitted v in Chasteau(v)ilain, q(u)e, promesses).

Review of Tomokiyo's unsolved list against the repo: his entry marks R9449 solved by him in 2025 and quotes the opening; the entry predates this project's attempt (6 Sept snapshot). The opening he quotes matches our reading's first line word for word (ct/no97_reading2.md L00). Prior claim missed by the 18 Sept search, which looked only for a published key.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry notes Tomokiyo had already solved it (2025); not a first break, dropped from the ciphertext-only list for Klaus Schmeh; marked independent re-solution.

Checked whether measure_reread.py counts sense: it counts hand grades H/C and only checks them against the key decode. New measure_sense.py tests every H/C word against an attested French lexicon (shared lang corpora fr-henri4, fr-1520s-diplomatic, fr-gutenberg) and the fr-1600-letters LM: 692/1,105 = 0.626 attested on the 22 Sept file (0.70 once single/double consonants are folded); the gap is spelling variants plus a few fragments.

Full-resolution IIIF f227 re-fetched, sheared -0.031, lines re-cropped and unread stretches re-read at 2x: L18 'l'effect du dict Chasteau(v)ilain', L12-13 'induiront et resolument', L04 'le mander' (not demander), L01 final gamma, L02 'pioniers' without the inserted c.
Figure 141 pooled over its three occurrences: 141+m(z) 'qu'ilz avoient fait', 141+J(s) 'qu'ils connoissent', 'affin qu'ils ne me delaissent': 141 = qu'il.

λ, γ, U, π, m̄ as nulls: of 37 occurrences all but two stand between complete words and the sentence reads without them (faire U passer, faire γ æ passer, fauldra λπ le remettre, satisfait m̄ du peu).

Joint coordinate-ascent solve of 17 special signs (single letters, nulls or common words) under fr-1600-letters on the whole text: the optimum changes with the per-char length penalty (1.6/2.0/2.4) and fills the text with 'pour'/'de'; per-sign lexicon test non-discriminating.
Context values ŧ/m̄/α + 'ien' = bien/rien/combien, E = la, 98 = ville: each fits some occurrences but not all, or other words fit equally; not counted.

measure_reread.py on the 5 Oct file: 861/1,102 = 0.781; fragments quelq, auld+is, promes fail the lexicon check and were downgraded to M: final 844/1,102 = 0.766 (letters 0.771, figures 24/38); measure_sense.py 787/1,102 = 0.714.

outcome.method_basis: The reciprocal letter-pair key was recovered by iterated local search on the eye transcription with no key known anywhere (DECODE, Tomokiyo, fr. 3995 key sheets ruled out); the page's clear text (Chasteauvillain) served only as a check, and three figures were read from context.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ct/no97_reread.txt (5 Oct 2026 pass) measured by measure_reread.py: cipher tokens (letter signs, special signs, nulls, figures; clear words excluded) in words graded H or C, 844/1,102; measure_sense.py lexicon check: 787/1,102 = 0.714 are attested French words, nulls, figures or joined fragments (difference = spelling variants)

gaps.item: Special signs ŧ, ⊙ (where not s), α, ꝗ, E, figure-4, Z, V and the words they sit in (about 60 tokens)
gaps.detail: No key survives; each occurs 1-12 times and no single value fits all occurrences; joint LM solve gave no stable assignment. λ, γ, U, π, m̄ settled as nulls 5 Oct.
Single letter, no key, no sibling in the same cipher; 141 = qu'il solved 5 Oct by pooling.

gaps.item: Garbled runs L12, L13, L20 (about 35 tokens)
gaps.detail: Re-read at full IIIF resolution 5 Oct: glyphs legible but the sequence does not decode under the pair key; L18 run resolved (l'effect du dict).

gaps.item: Fragments quelq, auld+is, promes (15 tokens, downgraded to M)
gaps.detail: Key decode is not a whole word; an abbreviation or special value is hidden.

outcome.notes: Re-read 22 Sept 2026 with the key in hand; the 18 Sept 'SOLVED' head and its 0.966 fraction_read (symbols given any value) and 0.7 estimate are superseded by the measured 0.715. Contributed 18 Sept by aryasn2026 (PR #4); re-read by Claude. 5 Oct 2026 push: 0.715 -> 0.766 (141 = qu'il pooled; λ γ U π m̄ nulls by distribution; image corrections in L01, L02, L04, L12-13, L18; three weak fragments downgraded). 95% not reachable from this copy.

prior.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved.htm, entry 'Duke of Lorraine (1592)', marked Solved: 'I solved this in 2025', quoting only the opening ("J'ay este infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution ...."); no key or text published. Present in the 6 Sept 2026 snapshot (targets/napoleon/unsolved.htm), before the 18 Sept attempt. DECODE R9449 still 'Non-decrypted'; no key anywhere.
